catalog_quote: It is further possible that such a shortening of the vowel resulted from the change of pitch accent to stress accent. Such a reconstruction would confirm the antiquity of the traditional position of the stress, namely penultimate.( 236) ... It is of course impossible to say whether [kl'] 'totally' (also [klh, klw] etc.) was, as in BA( 375), stressed penultimately or not. ... Is it at all possible to infer from this that the widely accepted development (/'alpu/ > /'alp/ > /'alep/ or /'alap/ > /'alep/ or /'alap/), namely the shift of penultimate to ultima stress, had already occurred? That is perhaps going a shade too far? ... Though the monophthongisation is confined to suffixed verb forms, its phonetic conditioning is not apparent: the presumed position of stress, for instance, varies.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding passage is present in the Muraoka-Porten djvu text we hold at the stated sections/footnotes (fn.105, fn.236, §18z with fn.375, jussive section), with only scanned noise on the Aramaic forms; the Phonology TOC confirms there is no stress section. (2) The deciding source is the standard reference grammar of Egyptian Aramaic (1998, HdO), the best available description; because the corpus is unvocalised, stress is unrecoverable except by reconstruction, which is exactly what the grammar says, so 'undetermined' is the correct coding and no better source can exist for the papyri themselves. sources.quote: §4a: 'Der Träger des Hauptdrucks ist, wie im Hebr., in den meisten Fällen die Ultima, oft auch die Paenultima: weiter nach vorn rückt der Druck nie.' §4l: 'Das Endergebnis der aram. Druckverschiebung stimmt insofern mit dem der hebr. überein, daß bei den meisten Wörtern die Ultima betont wurde, und daß Paenultimadruck nur in gewissen Fällen vorliegt' followed by an enumerated list (verb forms with suffixes -i, -u, -ta, -na, -a; 3fs of geminate verbs; forms with object/possessive suffixes -ni, -hi, -na; etc.). §4b-k reconstruct an older (Proto-Aramaic) stress further forward and a 'starke Druck
sources.locator: §4 Wortdruck, a (p.17) and l (pp.19-20); djvu the text layerand 2153-2200
sources.note: Glottolog files Biblical Aramaic under impe1235; this is the 'BA' comparandum Muraoka-Porten invoke and the only variety under this glottocode with an accent-marked (Tiberian) stress system: §4 'mostly ultima, often penult, never further forward'. Documents why 'undetermined' applies to the Egyptian consonantal corpus only; would seed a separate BA record if the catalog wants one.
